_meta.count_note: The brief asked for 50. The survey reached 69 because the pay-as-you-go hosts turned out to matter to the recommendation as overflow capacity, and cutting to exactly 50 would have meant dropping records that carry a lesson. 69 in, 20 scored, as asked.
_meta.note: One record per way of buying model capacity. A few records cover a family of near-identical vendors (e.g. `gpu-host-commodity` covers Parasail, GMICloud, AtlasCloud, Ionstream, StreamLake and DigitalOcean Gradient, which resell the same open weights at within ~2x of each other). Prices are the vendor's published USD figures on the date above; this market re-prices monthly, so treat every number as a reading, not a constant.

moderation_vocabulary.none: no provider-side classifier, and the served weights are uncensored or abliterated
moderation_vocabulary.model-only: no provider-side classifier; whatever the model was trained to refuse is all you get
moderation_vocabulary.configurable: provider runs filters but the developer can lower or disable them per request
moderation_vocabulary.provider-layer: provider runs its own classifier on requests and/or responses, not disableable
moderation_vocabulary.strict: provider-layer plus policy enforcement, account review, or org verification gates

candidates.name: OpenCode Go
candidates.quota: $12 per rolling 5h, $30/week, $60/month of provider-rate value; 6x the $10 fee
candidates.best_model: Kimi K3 / Grok 4.5 / Qwen3.8 Max / GLM-5.2
candidates.retention: 0-day for most models; Grok 4.5 and GPT 5.6 Luna retain 30 days; no training
candidates.lesson: Publishing the quota as dollars-of-provider-value instead of prompts is the single most honest limit design in this market. It is the only plan where you can compute your own request count for your own model mix before paying, and OpenCode publishes that table (31,650 DeepSeek V4 Flash requests per 5h down to 110 Kimi K3 requests per 5h).

candidates.name: Z.ai GLM Coding Plan
candidates.quota: 10,000 credits/week (Lite), 60,000 (Pro), 140,000 (Max); refresh every 7 days; Lite ~= 80 prompts/5h, ~400/week
candidates.web_tools: web search, web reading, repo access via bundled MCP, included at every tier
candidates.retention: CN jurisdiction; enterprise ZDR on request
candidates.lesson: The only plan in the survey that bundles web search and page reading as MCP tools at no extra cost on the entry tier. Everyone else either bills search per thousand queries or makes the harness bring its own.

candidates.name: Chutes
candidates.quota: 5x the plan's PAYG-equivalent value per month, metered on per-million-token model rates; sub-windows may apply per day or per few hours
candidates.lesson: Chutes abandoned a flat request-count subscription in February 2026 and said plainly why: token-agnostic request pricing is not viable once users point agents at it. Every request-count plan in this survey is living on borrowed time for the same reason.

candidates.name: Synthetic.new
candidates.quota: 500 messages per rolling 5h; low-cost tool calls metered at 0.1 credit so small calls barely count; 1 concurrent request per model; bundled Nomic embeddings unmetered
candidates.best_model: Kimi K3 / GLM / Qwen / DeepSeek (16 always-on open weights)
candidates.lesson: Discounting cheap tool calls to a tenth of a credit is the correct fix for agent workloads, where most calls are a grep or a file read rather than a reasoning turn. Unmetered embeddings matter more than they look: codebase indexing is what silently drains request-count plans.

candidates.name: Cerebras Code
candidates.quota: 24M tokens/day (Pro $50), 120M tokens/day (Max/Ultra $200)
candidates.lesson: The only plan quoted purely in tokens per day, which makes it the only one you can capacity-plan against directly. It buys throughput (up to ~2,000 tok/s) rather than intelligence, and has previously paused signups when demand outran the wafer capacity.

candidates.name: MiniMax Token Plan
candidates.lesson: The highest raw request ceiling per dollar of any plan here: 15,000 requests per 5 hours for $50. The catch is that M3 is a mid-tier model (Artificial Analysis intelligence 45.4), so the ceiling is generous precisely because each request is cheap to serve.

candidates.name: Kimi Code (Moonshot)
candidates.quota: 5h window refreshing every 7 days; Moderato $19 unlocks K3 with 60 agent credits and 2 concurrent tasks; Allegretto $39 lifts Kimi Code credits 1x->5x; Allegro $99; Vivace $199 adds 1M-token conversations
candidates.lesson: K3 is the strongest non-Western coding model in the survey (AA intelligence 60, tied with GLM-5.3) but also the most expensive open-weight model to serve at $3/$15. A subscription is the only sane way to touch it; at PAYG rates a Claude-Code-shaped workload costs more than Claude.

candidates.name: Nous Portal
candidates.quota: Plus $20 = $22 monthly credits, $10 rollover cap; Super $100 = $110 credits, $50 rollover; PAYG keys without a plan run 180 RPM / 720K TPM
candidates.web_tools: managed tool gateway: search, browser automation, code sandboxes, image/video/speech
candidates.lesson: The only vendor here that treats low refusal as a stated training objective rather than an absence of filtering: Hermes 4 is explicitly trained for steerability and neutral, user-directed behaviour. It also ships the only first-party browser-automation tool gateway. The credits are near face value (1.1x), so you are buying the gateway, not a discount.

candidates.name: Venice AI
candidates.quota: Pro $18 = unlimited text prompts in-app, 100 credits/mo for API; Pro Plus $68 = 7,500 credits; Max $200 = 22,500 credits. 100 credits = $1. Diem tokens give ~$1/day of compute refreshing daily
candidates.best_model: DeepSeek V4 Pro / Claude Sonnet 5 passthrough; Venice Uncensored 1.2 and Gemma 4 Uncensored in-house
candidates.web_tools: web search $10/1K requests, URL scraping $10/1K URLs (auto-detects up to 5 per request)
candidates.retention: local-only conversation storage, zero retention in private mode, TEE and E2EE options
candidates.lesson: The strongest privacy-plus-permissiveness combination in the survey, and it sells web scraping as a first-class metered product. But the unlimited part of Pro is the chat app; the API runs on a separate credit meter, which is the single most common misreading of this vendor's pricing.

candidates.name: StepFun Step Plan
candidates.lesson: The cheapest genuine entry point at $6.99, and it separates a subscription base URL from the PAYG one so the two meters never mix. The models are a tier below the leaders, which is the whole reason the price works.

candidates.name: Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan
candidates.lesson: Quoting the quota in tokens and then also in estimated tasks is the clearest limit disclosure of the Chinese plans. MiMo-V2.5 at $0.14/$0.28 with a 1M context and a $0.003 cache read is the cheapest million-token-context model in the survey.

candidates.name: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio Coding Plan
candidates.quota: Flat Coding Plan at CNY 200/month (~$28); Token Plan from CNY 198/seat/month; earlier tiers quoted 700/3,000/12,000 credits per 5h. Lite closed to new signups 2026-03-20
candidates.lesson: Alibaba resells its rivals — the Coding Plan covers Qwen, GLM, Kimi and MiniMax on one meter. It also shows how fast a free tier can vanish: the Qwen Code CLI's 2,000-requests/day free tier and the Qwen OAuth free tier were both killed in April 2026.

candidates.name: LLM Gateway DevPass
candidates.quota: $29/$79/$179 per month for roughly $87/$537 of provider-rate value; monthly reset
candidates.best_model: Claude Opus 5 / GPT-5.6 / Gemini 3.1 Pro plus open weights
candidates.retention: gateway logs; per-provider terms flow through
candidates.lesson: The only plan that puts closed frontier models and open-weight coders behind one flat ceiling, which is genuinely useful — but a gateway cannot loosen the upstream provider's guardrails. Buying Claude through DevPass buys Claude's refusal behaviour too.

candidates.name: Ollama Cloud
candidates.quota: Pro $20 = 50x Free, 3 concurrent models; Max $100 = 5x Pro, 10 concurrent (new signups paused); Team $25/seat, 5 seat minimum, ZDR
candidates.retention: no logging, no training on prompts or responses
candidates.lesson: Quotas expressed only as multiples of a free tier that is itself undefined are unplannable. The real value is the local/cloud continuum: identical model names run on your own box or theirs, which is the cleanest exit from vendor risk in this survey.

candidates.name: Featherless AI
candidates.quota: Chat $25 = unlimited tokens, 32K context, 4 concurrent units; Developer $50 = $50 of credits, 256K context, rollover, 1 agent environment
candidates.lesson: A 40,000-model catalog with first-class `uncensored` and `abliterated` filters is the widest permissive selection anywhere, and the $25 unlimited-token chat plan is real. But 32K context on that plan and unreliable tool calling across most of the catalog put it outside agentic coding.

candidates.name: Anthropic Claude Max (Claude Code)
candidates.quota: Max 5x and Max 20x; ~900 messages/5h at 20x; roughly 240-480 weekly Sonnet hours plus 24-40 Opus hours; exact token quotas never published
candidates.web_tools: web search $10/1K searches on the API
candidates.retention: no training on API/Code by default
candidates.lesson: This is the benchmark and it is also the reason the question exists. On 9 January 2026 Anthropic began rejecting subscription OAuth tokens outside its own client, with the error `This credential is only authorized for use with Claude Code`. A Max plan is no longer capacity you own; it is capacity you may use in one program.

candidates.name: OpenAI Codex via ChatGPT Plus/Pro
candidates.quota: Plus $20 limited; Pro $200 effectively unlimited Codex; ~49.1M tokens per dollar estimated at Pro
candidates.retention: training on by default for consumer tiers unless disabled
candidates.lesson: The best raw tokens-per-dollar of any subscription at the $200 tier, and unusable for this purpose for the same reason as Claude Max: the quota lives inside OpenAI's own client.

candidates.name: Google AI Pro / Ultra
candidates.quota: Enhanced Gemini CLI and Code Assist limits; per-model daily caps not published as fixed numbers
candidates.retention: consumer tiers may train; paid API does not
candidates.lesson: Gemini is the only major Western model whose safety filters the developer can lower per request, down to `OFF` on four harm categories. That control lives on the API, not on the subscription, which is a recurring shape: the permissive knob and the flat rate are sold separately.

candidates.name: GitHub Copilot Pro / Pro+
candidates.quota: Pro $10 = 300 premium requests/month; Pro+ $39 expanded
candidates.lesson: 300 premium requests a month is roughly two hours of agentic coding. Cheap headline, wrong shape.

candidates.name: Cursor Pro / Ultra
candidates.quota: Pro $20 includes ~$20 of usage; Ultra $200 includes ~$400
candidates.lesson: A 2x value multiple at the top tier is below every open-harness plan here, and it only spends inside one editor.

candidates.name: Windsurf Pro
candidates.quota: credit-based metering; free tier 25 prompt credits/month
candidates.lesson: Credit metering with no published per-model conversion rate is the least plannable limit design in the survey.

candidates.name: JetBrains AI Pro
candidates.quota: quota tied to JetBrains IDE seat
candidates.lesson: Bundling model capacity with an IDE seat means the capacity dies when you change editor.

candidates.name: Amazon Q Developer
candidates.quota: per-seat monthly agentic request allowance
candidates.lesson: AWS-shaped guardrails plus AWS-shaped identity. The strictest policy surface of any coding subscription here.

candidates.name: Cohere Command Code Pro / Max
candidates.quota: credit-based; Pro $15, Max $100
candidates.best_model: taste-1 plus Claude and GPT passthrough
candidates.lesson: Enterprise-first vendors sell governance as the product, which is exactly the axis this research is trying to minimise.

candidates.name: OpenCode Zen
candidates.quota: pure PAYG with workspace and per-member monthly caps; auto-reload at $5 balance, $20 default
candidates.best_model: Claude Opus 5 / GPT-5.6 Sol / Kimi K3 (50+ models)
candidates.lesson: The correct companion to a flat plan rather than a competitor to it: Go falls back to a Zen balance when the flat quota runs out, so the two together give a hard floor on cost and no hard ceiling on work.

candidates.name: DeepSeek API
candidates.quota: concurrency-limited rather than rate-limited: 2,500 concurrent for v4-flash, 500 for v4-pro; rates double during peak hours 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Mon-Fri
candidates.lesson: Selling concurrency instead of tokens per minute is the friendliest limit model for agents, which are bursty and parallel. DeepSeek is also the only lab that publishes an explicit off-peak discount, effectively a 50% overnight coupon for batch work.

candidates.name: Z.ai GLM API
candidates.quota: PAYG; GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.5-Flash are free
candidates.lesson: GLM-5.3-Flash at $0.075/$0.25 with a 1.31M context is the best price-to-context ratio in the entire survey, and two GLM Flash models are simply free.

candidates.name: Moonshot Kimi API
candidates.quota: tiered PAYG
candidates.lesson: A 943K max output token limit is the largest here by an order of magnitude and changes what a single agent turn can produce.

candidates.name: xAI Grok API
candidates.quota: PAYG; a 2x-priced fast lane exists at $4/$12
candidates.lesson: The highest-intelligence model in the survey served with no provider moderation layer (AA intelligence 60.9, ranked first on modelgrep's unmoderated list). It is the answer to `permissive and good` when price is not the constraint.

candidates.name: Anthropic Claude API
candidates.quota: Start/Build/Scale tiers: 1,000-10,000 RPM, 2M-10M ITPM, 400K-2M OTPM on Opus 5; monthly spend caps $500/$1,000/$200,000; cache reads do not count toward ITPM
candidates.lesson: Excluding cache reads from the rate limit is the most valuable limit-design decision any vendor here has made: at an 80% cache hit rate a 2M ITPM limit passes 10M tokens/minute. No Chinese lab matches this, and it is why Anthropic's published RPM looks stingier than it behaves.

candidates.name: OpenAI API
candidates.quota: Tiers 1-5 gated on cumulative spend ($5 to $1,000) with monthly usage limits from $100 to $200,000
candidates.retention: no training on API by default
candidates.lesson: GPT-5.6 Luna at $0.20/$1.20 with a 1.05M context is the cheapest frontier-brand model in the survey after the July 2026 price cut, and it is where the mainstream price floor of ~$0.20/M now sits.

candidates.name: Google Gemini API
candidates.quota: spend-based usage tiers; limits are account-specific and only visible in AI Studio, not published as fixed tables
candidates.lesson: Four harm categories are developer-adjustable across five thresholds down to `OFF`; only child-safety protections are fixed. Google warns that loosened settings may trigger review, so this is permissiveness you configure and account for, not permissiveness you are given.

candidates.name: OpenRouter
candidates.quota: PAYG with a ~5% credit fee; per-model and per-provider routing controls
candidates.lesson: The best instrument in the market rather than the best product: its public models API exposes `is_moderated` per endpoint, and 291 of 417 models are served unmoderated. It is also the only place to see that the same model is served at different quantisations by different hosts.

candidates.name: Commodity open-weight hosts (Parasail, GMICloud, AtlasCloud, Ionstream, StreamLake, DigitalOcean Gradient, CoreWeave)
candidates.quota: PAYG; uptime observed 92-100% over 30 days on OpenRouter
candidates.best_model: DeepSeek V4 Pro / Kimi K3 / MiniMax M3
candidates.lesson: The same model name spans a 2.2x price range and fp4/fp8/bf16 quantisations across these hosts. Cheapest-endpoint routing is silently a quality decision, and OpenRouter is the only place that shows you which one you are getting.

candidates.name: Together AI
candidates.quota: PAYG with tiered RPM
candidates.lesson: Observed 92.6% uptime on DeepSeek V4 Pro over 30 days, the worst of the major hosts in that sample. Premium pricing does not buy availability.

candidates.name: Fireworks AI
candidates.quota: PAYG; enterprise dedicated capacity
candidates.lesson: Serves the same model at three different prices ($3.00, $3.30, $4.50 input for Kimi K3) depending on the tier you land on, which makes headline price comparisons across hosts unreliable.

candidates.name: DeepInfra
candidates.quota: PAYG, among the cheapest per token
candidates.lesson: Cheapest MiniMax M3 endpoint at $0.28/$1.10, but caps Kimi K3 max output at 16K against Moonshot's 943K. Output ceilings, not prices, are where budget hosts actually differ.

candidates.name: Groq
candidates.quota: free tier with hard daily caps; developer tier PAYG
candidates.lesson: Speed without a flagship. Fast inference on mid-tier weights does not substitute for a frontier coder, however good the tokens-per-second number looks.

candidates.name: Novita AI
candidates.quota: PAYG
candidates.lesson: 99.98% observed uptime on DeepSeek V4 Pro, the best of the mid-price hosts. Reliability and price are not correlated in this tier.

candidates.name: SiliconFlow
candidates.quota: PAYG
candidates.lesson: Documented as not supporting thinking-model variants, which quietly removes the reasoning modes that make these models competitive at coding.

candidates.name: Nebius AI Studio
candidates.quota: PAYG
candidates.lesson: The only EU-jurisdiction open-weight host of scale, which is the answer when the objection to the cheap tier is data residency rather than price.

candidates.name: SambaNova Cloud
candidates.quota: PAYG; 100% observed uptime on MiniMax M3
candidates.lesson: Custom silicon at 2x the commodity price for the same weights. You pay for latency, and only latency.

candidates.name: Phala Network (TEE inference)
candidates.quota: PAYG
candidates.lesson: Trusted-execution inference is the only technical answer to `the host can read my prompts`, as opposed to the contractual answer everyone else sells. Priced at parity with Moonshot's own endpoint, so the attestation is free.

candidates.name: NanoGPT
candidates.quota: $12/mo optional subscription; otherwise list-price PAYG with no markup, deposits from $0.10 in crypto
candidates.lesson: Charges list price with no markup and monetises pinning (+5%) and BYOK (5%) instead. Anonymous crypto onboarding with no published retention policy is a privacy story that only works in one direction.

candidates.name: Arli AI
candidates.quota: unlimited generations with concurrency caps per tier
candidates.lesson: Genuinely unlimited and genuinely uncensored, on models that cannot call a tool or hold a codebase. This is the clearest illustration that the uncensored-hosting market and the agentic-coding market barely overlap.

candidates.name: Infermatic
candidates.quota: unlimited requests, concurrency-capped
candidates.lesson: Same shape as Arli: flat-rate unlimited works commercially only because the models are small enough that unlimited is affordable.

candidates.name: uncensored.chat / abliteration.ai / unfil.ai / NinjaChat
candidates.quota: not published
candidates.best_model: Dolphin 3, Hermes, abliterated Llama and Qwen variants
candidates.lesson: This whole segment markets the absence of a filter as the product and publishes neither limits nor retention. Even their own marketing concedes that removing refusal training does not change what is lawful, and that reputable hosts keep hard policy lines regardless of model.

candidates.name: Wiro AI
candidates.quota: PAYG
candidates.best_model: Qwen 3.8 27B Uncensored, Seed V2 Pro Uncensored, Grok 4.20 2M context
candidates.lesson: Advertises uncensored variants of models whose licences and provenance it does not document. Serving `Grok 4.20` at 2M context is a claim no first-party source supports.

candidates.name: Uncensored fine-tune families (TheDrummer, Sao10K, Anthracite Magnum, MythoMax, Undi95)
candidates.quota: host-dependent
candidates.lesson: Measured across OpenRouter's catalogue, essentially none of this family supports tool calling and most cap at 32K-131K context. They are the models people mean by `uncensored`, and they are structurally incapable of the two jobs in this brief.

candidates.name: Nous Hermes 4 (405B / 70B)
candidates.quota: host-dependent
candidates.lesson: The only widely-served model trained deliberately for low refusal and neutral, user-directed behaviour rather than merely lacking a filter. Its OpenRouter endpoints still advertise no tool support, so the capability has to come from the Nous Portal gateway rather than the model.

candidates.name: Self-hosted vLLM / SGLang on rented GPUs
candidates.quota: bounded only by the GPU; RTX Pro 6000 96GB rents at ~$1.80/hour on Chutes, i.e. ~$1,300/month continuous
candidates.best_model: any open weight you can fit
candidates.lesson: The true zero-guardrail option, and the arithmetic kills it: continuous rental of one 96GB card costs more per month than the most expensive subscription here and still will not hold a 2.8T-parameter model. Self-hosting wins on control and loses on every other axis at one-person scale.

candidates.name: Ollama / LM Studio local
candidates.quota: unbounded; needs 32K+ context minimum for coding agents
candidates.best_model: qwen3-coder, glm-4.7, minimax-m2.1 at consumer quantisations
candidates.lesson: Free, private and unfiltered, running models several capability tiers below what a coding agent needs. Useful as the fallback that always works when a vendor bans you, not as the daily driver.

candidates.name: Mistral API
candidates.quota: Le Chat Pro $14.99/mo; API PAYG
candidates.lesson: Ships a `safe_prompt` flag that is off by default, making it the most permissive Western lab by policy rather than by omission. The models are a tier below the coding leaders, which is why that permissiveness rarely gets used.

candidates.name: ByteDance Seed / Volcano Engine
candidates.quota: PAYG
candidates.lesson: A dedicated coding model (Seed 2.0 Code) at $0.50/$3.00 that almost nobody outside China evaluates. Its absence from Western comparisons is a distribution fact, not a quality finding.

candidates.name: Tencent Hunyuan
candidates.quota: PAYG
candidates.lesson: Hy3 appears inside OpenCode Go's bundle at 4,300 requests per 5 hours, which is where this family is actually worth using: as cheap bulk capacity someone else has already integrated.

candidates.name: Baidu ERNIE
candidates.quota: PAYG
candidates.lesson: 123K context and no tool calling in 2026 is not a coding option. Baidu also resells DeepSeek V4 Pro, which is the only reason its endpoint appears in agent routing tables.

candidates.name: Amazon Bedrock
candidates.quota: per-region provisioned or on-demand quotas
candidates.lesson: Adds a configurable Guardrails product on top of whatever the model already refuses, and charges a ~10% premium over the first-party endpoint for Grok. Cloud marketplaces sell more policy, not less.

candidates.name: Requesty
candidates.quota: PAYG with routing and spend controls
candidates.lesson: Gateways compete on routing policy and spend controls now, not on catalogue size; every one of them has essentially the same models.

candidates.name: iFlow CLI
candidates.quota: free tier with undisclosed daily caps
candidates.lesson: Free CLIs backed by undisclosed quotas and undisclosed retention are the cheapest way to find out that your prompts were the payment.

candidates.name: Poolside Laguna
candidates.quota: PAYG; free tiers of laguna-s and laguna-xs on OpenRouter
candidates.lesson: A US lab shipping a purpose-built coding model at $0.09/$0.18 with a 1M context and a genuinely free tier, unmoderated. The cheap-and-permissive tier is no longer exclusively Chinese.

candidates.name: Morph / Relace (fast-apply models)
candidates.quota: PAYG
candidates.lesson: Edit-application is now a separate purchasable model class. Pairing a cheap frontier planner with a dedicated fast-apply model is the cost structure the IDE vendors actually run, and nothing stops a self-assembled harness from copying it.

candidates.name: Perplexity Sonar API
candidates.quota: Pro $20 includes $5/mo API credit; Max $200
candidates.web_tools: search is the product; citations returned inline
candidates.lesson: The only vendor where retrieval is priced into the token rate rather than billed per query. For a read-only web agent that is strictly cheaper than a general model plus $10-14 per thousand searches; for an agent that must also act, the missing tool calling is fatal.

candidates.name: Warp
candidates.quota: request-based tiers per seat
candidates.lesson: A terminal is not more portable than an editor if the model credentials are still bound to the vendor's binary.

candidates.name: Factory Droid
candidates.quota: token-based allowances per tier
candidates.lesson: Reselling frontier models under a flat rate inherits their refusal behaviour exactly. A wrapper cannot be more permissive than what it wraps.

candidates.name: Kilo Code
candidates.quota: BYOK or Kilo credits
candidates.lesson: Listed to make the boundary explicit: harnesses are not capacity. Kilo, Cline, Roo and OpenCode itself are all clients that any of the plans above can drive.

candidates.name: Aion Labs
candidates.quota: host-dependent
candidates.lesson: One of the very few unmoderated model families that does support tool calling, which makes it the exception that proves how rare that combination is outside the Chinese labs.

candidates.name: inclusionAI Ling
candidates.quota: host-dependent
candidates.lesson: The cheapest tool-capable model with a 262K context anywhere: $0.021/$0.063. At these rates the token cost of an agent stops mattering and orchestration overhead becomes the entire bill.

candidates.name: Thinking Machines Inkling
candidates.quota: free tier on OpenRouter
candidates.lesson: A 1.05M-context, 262K-output, tool-capable, unmoderated model at zero cost. Free frontier-adjacent tiers exist right now and none of them have ever survived contact with sustained agent traffic.

candidates.name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3
candidates.quota: free and paid tiers on OpenRouter
candidates.lesson: A US-origin, unmoderated, tool-capable 550B model with a 1M context and free variants. For anyone whose objection to the cheap tier is Chinese jurisdiction rather than price, this is the closest substitute.
